etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: First attested in 1535, from Latin recantare (“to sing back, reecho, sing again, repeat in singing, recant, recall, revoke, charm back or away”), from re- (“back”) + canto (“to chant, to sing”), frequentative of cano.
senses: (ambitransitive) To withdraw or repudiate a statement or opinion formerly expressed, especially formally and publicly.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
senses: To give a new cant (slant, angle) to something, in particular railway track on a curve.
